MiDAS_course_2025

Miriam Peces, Sofie Zacho Vestergaard, Marta Nierychlo

2025-06-02, Aalborg, Denmark

Questions for the MiDAS course - ampvis hands on. Whenever you encounter “…” it means you should fill something in there.

Only do ONCE!!!!

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("kasperskytte/ampvis2")
install.packages("tidyverse")

Load the packages

library(ampvis2)
library(tidyverse)

Set your working directory - only if you did not open script from the downloaded folder

#setwd("")

Load the data into an ampvis object

d_midas <- amp_load(otutable = "data/ASVtable.tsv",
              taxonomy = "data/ASVs.R1.midas53.sintax",
              metadata = "data/metadata_midascourse.txt")

Inspect the data - get a summary of the ampvis object

d_midas
## ampvis2 object with 3 elements. 
## Summary of OTU table:
##      Samples         OTUs  Total#Reads    Min#Reads    Max#Reads Median#Reads 
##          141        12229      6316036          886       127366        42719 
##    Avg#Reads 
##     44794.58 
## 
## Assigned taxonomy:
##       Kingdom        Phylum         Class         Order        Family 
##   12229(100%) 12159(99.43%) 12117(99.08%) 12019(98.28%) 11839(96.81%) 
##         Genus       Species 
## 11114(90.88%)  8897(72.75%) 
## 
## Metadata variables: 5 
##  SampleID, SampleContent, SampleSite, SampleDate, Month

Investigate rarefaction curve

amp_rarecurve(d_midas, 
              color_by = 'SampleSite') +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 10000)

plot the number of reads for each sample

ggplot( amp_alpha_diversity(d_midas))+
  geom_point(aes(x= SampleID, y = Reads, color=SampleSite)) +
  facet_grid(~ SampleSite, scales = 'free_x', space = 'free') +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, size=6, vjust= 0.5))

Filter data: Remove low read samples and normalise data

dsn_midas <- amp_subset_samples(d_midas,
                                minreads = 10000, # remove samples with less than 10000 reads
                                normalise = TRUE)
## 2 samples and 11 OTUs have been filtered 
## Before: 141 samples and 12229 OTUs
## After: 139 samples and 12218 OTUs

Questions to answer

Q1 What are the top 25 most abundant genera? hint: look into amp_heatmap()

amp_heatmap(dsn_midas,
            normalise = F,
            group_by = 'SampleSite',
            tax_show = 25,
            tax_aggregate = 'Genus',
            color_vector = c('white', 'darkred'))
## Warning in scale_fill_gradientn(colours = color.pal, trans = plot_colorscale, :
## log-10 transformation introduced infinite values.

Q2 What are the top 25 most abundant species? And what genera are these belonging to (plot these with the species)?

amp_heatmap(dsn_midas,
            normalise = F,
            group_by = 'SampleSite',
            tax_show = 25,
            tax_aggregate = 'Species',
            tax_add = 'Genus',
            color_vector = c('white', 'darkred'))
## Warning in scale_fill_gradientn(colours = color.pal, trans = plot_colorscale, :
## log-10 transformation introduced infinite values.

Addition Q3 - sort by a specific plant

amp_heatmap(dsn_midas,
            normalise = F,
            group_by = 'SampleSite',
            tax_show = 25,
            tax_aggregate = 'Species',
            sort_by = 'WWTP_C',
            tax_add = 'Genus',
            color_vector = c('white', 'darkred'))
## Warning in scale_fill_gradientn(colours = color.pal, trans = plot_colorscale, :
## log-10 transformation introduced infinite values.

Q3 Try to save the heatmap from before

heatmap <- amp_heatmap(dsn_midas,
            normalise = F,
            group_by = 'SampleSite',
            tax_show = 25,
            tax_aggregate = 'Species',
            tax_add = 'Genus',
            color_vector = c('white', 'darkred'))

ggsave("heatmap.png", heatmap,
       width = 8, height = 6 #change to fit your needs
       ) 
## Warning in scale_fill_gradientn(colours = color.pal, trans = plot_colorscale, :
## log-10 transformation introduced infinite values.

Q4. Perform an ordination to compare the microbial structures of the different WWTPs.

amp_ordinate(data = dsn_midas, 
             transform = "Hellinger", 
             type = "PCA",
             sample_color_by = "SampleSite") +
  scale_colour_viridis_d() + # example how to customise with ggplot
  theme_bw() # example how to customise with ggplot
## 10898 OTUs not present in more than 0.1% relative abundance in any sample have been filtered 
## Before: 12218 OTUs
## After: 1320 OTUs

Compare to silva taxonomy Q5 How many of the ASVs are classified at genus and species level using silva? hint: amp_load() with silva tax

d_silva <- amp_load(otutable = "data/ASVtable.tsv",
              taxonomy = "data/ASVs_SILVA_138.2.R1.sintax",
              metadata = "data/metadata_midascourse.txt") 

dsn_silva <- amp_subset_samples(d_silva,
                                minreads = 10000, # remove samples with less than 10000 reads
                                normalise = TRUE)

## After: 139 samples and 12218 OTUs

Q6 What are the most abundant 25 genera using silva? Compare to MiDAS taxonomic assignment

amp_heatmap(dsn_silva,
            normalise = F,
            group_by = 'SampleSite',
            tax_show = 25,
            tax_aggregate = 'Species',

Q7 Make a timeseries plot for Ca. Phosphoribacter and Ca. Accumulibacter in Randers? hint: look into amp_subset_taxa(), amp_subset_sample(), amp_time_series()

subset <- amp_subset_taxa(data = dsn_midas, tax_vector = c("g__Ca_Phosphoribacter", "g__Ca_Accumulibacter")) %>% 
  amp_subset_samples(SampleSite == "WWTP_C")
## Warning: One or more samples have 0 total reads
## 12169 OTUs have been filtered 
## Before: 12218 OTUs
## After: 49 OTUs
## 88 samples and 3 OTUs have been filtered 
## Before: 139 samples and 49 OTUs
## After: 51 samples and 46 OTUs
subset$metadata$SampleDate <- as.Date(subset$metadata$SampleDate, format = c("%d/%m/%Y"))
  
amp_time_series(subset,
                time_variable = "SampleDate", 
                tax_aggregate = "Genus",
                normalise = FALSE)

Q8 Make a timeseries plot for a species and plant of your choice

subset <- amp_subset_taxa(data = dsn_midas, tax_vector = c("g__Zoogloea")) %>% 
  amp_subset_samples(SampleSite == "WWTP_C")
## Warning: One or more samples have 0 total reads
## 12209 OTUs have been filtered 
## Before: 12218 OTUs
## After: 9 OTUs
## 88 samples and 0 OTUs have been filtered 
## Before: 139 samples and 9 OTUs
## After: 51 samples and 9 OTUs
subset$metadata$SampleDate <- as.Date(subset$metadata$SampleDate, format = c("%d/%m/%Y"))
  
amp_time_series(subset,
                time_variable = "SampleDate", 
                tax_aggregate = "Genus",
                normalise = FALSE)

extra questions

Qe1-a Make an ordination plot for all plants - Try different ordinations, e.g PCoA based on bray-curtis distance hint: look into amp_ordinate()

amp_ordinate(dsn_midas, 
             sample_color_by = 'SampleSite')
## 10898 OTUs not present in more than 0.1% relative abundance in any sample have been filtered 
## Before: 12218 OTUs
## After: 1320 OTUs

amp_ordinate(dsn_midas, 
             sample_color_by = 'SampleSite',
             type = 'PCoA',
             distmeasure = 'Bray',
             sample_colorframe = T,
             sample_colorframe_label = 'SampleSite')
## 10898 OTUs not present in more than 0.1% relative abundance in any sample have been filtered 
## Before: 12218 OTUs
## After: 1320 OTUs
## Warning: Using both transformation AND a distance measure is not recommended
## for distance-based ordination (nMDS/PCoA). If this is not deliberate, consider
## transform = "none".

Qe1-b Make an ordination plot for a plant of your choice to explore the temporal dynamics of the overall microbial structure hint: subset first for your chosen WWTP

plant_subset <- amp_subset_samples(dsn_midas, SampleSite == "WWTP_A")
## 100 samples and 4784 OTUs have been filtered 
## Before: 139 samples and 12218 OTUs
## After: 39 samples and 7434 OTUs
plant_subset$metadata$SampleDate <- as.Date(plant_subset$metadata$SampleDate, format = c("%d/%m/%Y"))


amp_ordinate(plant_subset, 
             sample_trajectory = "SampleDate",
             sample_color_by = "SampleDate",
             sample_label_by = "Month")
## 7021 OTUs not present in more than 0.1% relative abundance in any sample have been filtered 
## Before: 7434 OTUs
## After: 413 OTUs

Qe3 Which genera within Proteobacteria are the most abundant across all samples? hint: look into amp_subset_taxa()

proteo <- amp_subset_taxa(dsn_midas,
                          tax_vector = 'p__Proteobacteria',
                          normalise = F)
## 9148 OTUs have been filtered 
## Before: 12218 OTUs
## After: 3070 OTUs
amp_heatmap(proteo, 
             normalise = F,
            tax_aggregate = 'Genus',
            group_by = 'SampleSite',
            tax_show = 25)
## Warning in scale_fill_gradientn(colours = color.pal, trans = plot_colorscale, :
## log-10 transformation introduced infinite values.

Qe4 Make alpha diversity analysis for the data (remember to rarefy at the same time) hint: look into amp_alpha_diversity()

alpha <- amp_alpha_diversity(amp_subset_samples(d_midas,
                                minreads = 10000, normalise = F),
                            rarefy = 10000)
## 2 samples and 11 OTUs have been filtered 
## Before: 141 samples and 12229 OTUs
## After: 139 samples and 12218 OTUs
## Warning: The chosen rarefy size (10000) is smaller than the smallest amount of
## reads in any sample (14136).
ggplot(alpha) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x=SampleSite, y = uniqueOTUs, fill = SampleSite),
              )

ggplot(alpha) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(x=SampleSite, y = Shannon, fill = SampleSite)) +
  geom_point(aes(x=SampleSite, y = Shannon, fill = SampleSite),
             shape=21, position = position_jitter(width = 0.1))
